[tool_result Read] 1	# Twin Manager — Documentation
2	
3	Twin is a two-pane file manager for the terminal in the Norton / Midnight Commander tradition: you
4	pick files in one pane and act on them towards the other. It is Linux-focused.
5	
6	## Requirements
7	
8	- Linux. Mounted drives are read from `/proc/mounts`, and unmounting runs `umount`.
9	- `xdg-open` to open files with their default application.
10	- For Copy Path: `wl-copy` (Wayland), `xclip` or `xsel`. Without any of them Twin sends the path
11	  to the terminal with the OSC 52 escape sequence, which most current terminals put on the
12	  clipboard.
13	
14	## Running
15	
16	```bash
17	go run .
18	```
19	
20	or build the `twin` binary first:
21	
22	```bash
23	go build .
24	./twin
25	```
26	
27	Both panes start in the current directory, with the left pane active.
28	
29	## The screen
30	
31	- **Panes.** Each pane shows its directory path on the first line and its entries below:
32	  directories first (in blue), then files, each group sorted by name in byte order (capitals
33	  before lowercase). Hidden files are always shown. Every directory except `/` starts with a
34	  `..` entry that leads to the parent. Symbolic links end in `@`; a link to a directory is listed
35	  with the directories and is entered like one.
36	- **Active pane.** The active pane has a blue border, the other a grey one. Copy and move always
37	  go from the active pane into the other pane's directory.
38	- **Status bar.** Shows the name, permissions and modification time of the entry under the
39	  cursor, the quick-search query, the questions Twin asks (overwrite? delete?) and, in red, the
40	  latest error.
41	- **Hint bar.** Lists the Alt shortcuts.
42	
43	## Keys
44	
45	### Shortcuts
46	
47	Every shortcut has an Alt binding; the classic ones also answer to the Midnight Commander
48	function key.
49	
50	<!-- shortcuts: kept in sync with keys.go by docs_test.go -->
51	| Key | F-key | Action |
52	| --- | --- | --- |
53	| `Alt+V` | `F3` | View the file under the cursor |
54	| `Alt+C` | `F5` | Copy to the other pane |
55	| `Alt+M` | `F6` | Move to the other pane |
56	| `Alt+N` | `F7` | Create a folder in the active pane |
57	| `Alt+D` | `F8` | Delete (permanently) |
58	| `Alt+P` | `F9` | Copy the full path to the clipboard |
59	| `Alt+Q` | `F10` | Quit, without asking |
60	| `Ctrl+C` | | Quit (same as Alt+Q) |
61	| `Tab` | | Switch the active pane |
62	| `Insert` | | Select or deselect the entry under the cursor, then move down |
63	| `Alt+F` | | Favorites and drives |
64	| `Alt+A` | | Add a directory to the favorites |
65	| `Alt+I` | | Sync panes: open the active pane's directory in the other pane |
66	| `Alt+O` | | Open the directory under the cursor in the other pane |
67	| `Alt+L` | | Error log |
68	
69	### Moving around
70	
71	| Key | Action |
72	| --- | --- |
73	| `↑` `↓` | Move the cursor |
74	| `PgUp` `PgDn` | Move the cursor by a pane's height |
75	| `Home` `End` | First or last entry |
76	| `Enter` | Enter a directory, or open a file with `xdg-open`. On `..`, go up with the cursor on the directory you came from |
77	| any letter, digit or symbol | Quick search |
78	| `Esc` | Clear the quick search |
79	
80	### Quick search
81	
82	Typing in a pane jumps to a match; there is nothing to open first. Each character extends the
83	query, which is shown in the status bar. The cursor jumps to the first entry whose name starts
84	with the query, ignoring case; if there is none, to the first entry that contains the query's
85	characters in order (`cmg` finds `commands.go`). Esc, ↑/↓, PgUp/PgDn and Enter clear the
86	query. Backspace does not edit it: press Esc and type again.
87	
88	## Working with files
89	
90	### Which files an operation acts on
91	
92	Copy, Move, Delete and Copy Path act on the selected entries of the active pane, or on the entry
93	under the cursor when nothing is selected. Select with Insert. The `..` entry cannot be selected
94	and is never copied, moved or deleted. Starting a copy or move, or confirming a delete, clears
95	the selection.
96	
97	### Copy and Move
98	
99	Alt+C (F5) copies and Alt+M (F6) moves into the other pane's directory. Twin first checks the
100	whole batch without touching anything:
101	
102	- **Refused entries** are reported as errors while the rest of the batch goes ahead: `..`, an
103	  entry copied or moved onto itself (both panes in the same directory, or the same file reached
104	  through a hard link or symlink), and a directory copied or moved into itself or one of its
105	  subdirectories.
106	- **Conflicts.** For every entry whose name already exists at the destination, the status bar
107	  asks `Overwrite NAME? (y/n/A/s)`:
108	
109	  | Key | Answer |
110	  | --- | --- |
111	  | `y` | Overwrite this one |
112	  | `n` | Skip this one |
113	  | `A` | Overwrite this one and every remaining conflict |
114	  | `s` | Skip this one and every remaining conflict |
115	  | `Esc` | Cancel the whole batch: nothing is copied or moved, not even the entries without a conflict |
116	
117	  Nothing is written until every conflict is answered; then the whole batch runs at once.
118	
119	Overwriting a directory merges into it: files inside it with the same names are overwritten
120	without further questions, and files that exist only at the destination stay.
121	
122	**Copying** keeps permissions and modification times. Each file is written to a temporary file
123	next to its destination and renamed into place, so an overwritten file is either replaced whole
124	or left as it was. Replacing makes it a new file: it is owned by you, loses its ACLs and extended
125	attributes, a symlink at the destination is replaced instead of written through, and other hard
126	links to the old file keep the old content. Symbolic links are copied as links to the same
127	target, never followed. FIFOs, sockets and device files are refused. A directory is never copied
128	or moved through a symlink at the destination.
129	
130	**Moving** renames within a filesystem. Across filesystems (to a USB drive, for example) Twin
131	copies, flushes the copy to disk, and only then removes the source. I

215	  letters are dropped, and paste is ignored.
216	- Delete is permanent; there is no trash and no undo.
217	- Copy and move show no progress and cannot be cancelled.
218	- Nothing is saved between sessions, favorites included, and there is no config file.
219	- Preview reads the whole file before cutting it at 100 KB, so previewing a huge file is slow.
220	- Long names and paths are not shortened to fit the pane.
221	
222	## Under the hood
223	
224	Twin is written in Go with [Bubble Tea](https://github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea), an Elm-style
225	Model-View-Update framework, and [Lip Gloss](https://github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss) for
226	styling. The whole state is one `model`; `Update` turns key presses and results into a new model;
227	`View` renders it. Anything that touches the disk runs in a command off the UI thread and reports
228	back with a message, so the interface does not freeze.
229	
230	| File | Contents |
231	| --- | --- |
232	| `model.go` | The `model` and `pane` state, and the initial state |
233	| `update.go` | `Update`: the dialogs, the shortcuts, results of commands, and pane navigation |
234	| `commands.go` | Commands that do I/O and return a message |
235	| `msg.go` | The message types |
236	| `fs.go` | Filesystem helpers: listing, the copy/move plan, copy, move, drives |
237	| `keys.go` | The key map: every shortcut, its Alt binding and F-key alias |
238	| `view.go`, `styles.go` | Rendering and its styles |
239	| `utils.go` | Fuzzy matching and text wrapping |
240	
241	Copy and move are planned, resolved and only then executed. `planBatch` sorts a batch into clean
242	entries, conflicts and refused entries without touching anything; `Update` asks about each
243	conflict; `transferFiles` runs the batch and re-checks the same safety rules.
244	
245	The shortcut table above mirrors `keys.go`; `docs_test.go` fails when they disagree, so a new or
246	changed shortcut needs a matching row. For development commands and CI see the
247	[README](README.md).
